title: Consolidate the Atlas into per-Scope and per-Artifact files
body:
Consolidates the Atlas content tree from 11,335 `content/<segments>/document.md` files plus 3,851 generated `_index.md` files into **18 composed markdown files**: one per top-level Scope (`A.0`–`A.6`), and one per Agent Artifact.

## No content change — structure only, and you can check it in two commands

```bash
git checkout <this-branch> && python sync/atlas_source.py --input content --output /tmp/after.md
git checkout main          && python sync/compose.py      --input content --output /tmp/before.md
cmp /tmp/before.md /tmp/after.md
```

They are byte-identical at **3,756,751 characters**. The validator passes on the composed output with 0 errors (the single cross-reference warning is present identically before and after).

## Updated after review

Two changes since the first version, both from @0xldr's review:

**`A.6.1.2` is no longer a standalone file.** It is a Section, structurally identical to its sibling `A.6.1.1`, and both now sit in `A.6 - The-Agent-Scope.md` with the rest of the Agent Scope spine. It was separate only because reassembly concatenated whole files in bucket order, which required every bucket to occupy one unbroken run of the composed stream — and `A.6.1.2` is emitted after the Prime Agent Artifacts. Reassembly now orders documents rather than buckets, so that constraint no longer exists.

**Each Executor Agent has its own file**, matching the Prime Agents. There are three:

| | |
|---|---|
| `A.6.1.2.1` | Operational Executor Agent Amatsu |
| `A.6.1.2.2` | Operational Executor Agent Ozone |
| `A.6.1.2.3` | Core Council Executor Agent 1 |

Also from the review: `sync/compose_and_hash.py` and `sync/hash.py` are removed — nothing referenced either. `sync/decompose.py` is kept: `decompose_multi.py` and `partition.py` both import it, and it is reached on every PR through `atlas_source.py`.

## Why

The hard **300-file GitHub diff cap**. This is not theoretical — the current `proposal/2026-08-10` branch touches **228 files** under today's layout, 76% of the cap, and **7** under this one. File count scales with an edit's *structural reach*, not its semantic size, so a pure relocation can cost hundreds of files while changing no text.

| | files changed |
|---|---|
| today | 228 |
| after this PR | 7 |

## The layout

```
content/A.0 - Atlas-Preamble.md                 content/A.6.1.1.1 - Spark.md       657 KB
content/A.1 - The-Governance-Scope.md   572 KB  content/A.6.1.1.2 - Grove.md       576 KB
content/A.2 - The-Support-Scope.md      589 KB  content/A.6.1.1.3 - Keel.md        254 KB
content/A.3 - The-Stability-Scope.md    287 KB  ...through A.6.1.1.8
content/A.4 - The-Protocol-Scope.md      86 KB  content/A.6 - The-Agent-Scope.md
content/A.5 - The-Accessibility-Scope.md        content/A.6.1.2.1 - ...Amatsu.md
                                                content/A.6.1.2.2 - ...Ozone.md
                                                content/A.6.1.2.3 - ...Core-Council-Executor-Agent-1.md
```

Largest file is 33% of GitHub's soft render threshold. Files stay **inside `content/`** deliberately: the downstream sync workflow pulls `content/`, CI guards key on `content/**`, and the portal fetches a tarball and reads `content/`. Keeping the directory name means none of those change.

## Tooling

| | |
|---|---|
| `sync/partition.py` | the bucketing rule. Consumes compose's existing walk via a new `compose_segments()` rather than adding a fifth tree-walker to the four that already exist |
| `sync/decompose_multi.py` | reassembly, then the existing `decompose()` unchanged |
| `sync/atlas_source.py` | one entry point composing from **either** layout, so no consumer needs to know two layouts exist |
| `sync/migrate_branch.py` | migrates an in-flight edit branch by recomputing its consolidated form — authors re-apply nothing |

Two invariants hold against the real tree:

```
reassemble(split(x))      == compose(x)
decompose_multi(split(x)) == decompose(compose(x))
```

Nothing generated is committed — no manifest, no index files. Reassembly derives order from document numbers rather than from file order, so there is nothing to conflict on when two edit branches touch different Scopes, and no configuration to update when a new Agent is onboarded. `split()` verifies that the partition it produced reassembles byte-identically.

## Three silent failures fixed, without which this cutover would have been invisible

1. **`validate-atlas.yml` called `sync/compose.py` directly.** Post-consolidation that walks for `document.md`, finds none, writes **0 bytes and exits 0** — and the validator **passes on a 0-byte file**. There is no guard anywhere in this workflow to catch it, so every Atlas PR would have gone green having validated nothing, indefinitely. Now routed through `atlas_source`, which raises rather than returning empty.

2. **`compose.py` now refuses to write or hash an empty composition**, on `--output` and `--check` alike. Previously an empty composition compared against an empty expected file printed `ROUNDTRIP OK` and exited 0.

3. **`composed-atlas.md` is now gitignored.** The composed artifact was committed twice by accident during the previous migration.

## In-flight branches

`sync/migrate_branch.py` recomputes a branch's consolidated form; the migrated diff is `split(head)` against `split(main)`. It touches no working tree (git plumbing only), tags `<branch>-pre-cutover` before creating anything so rollback is one force-push, and has a `--report-only` rehearsal mode.

Rehearsed read-only against all **27** open pull requests touching `content/`, each verified byte-identical: **27 of 27 clean**, none needing author intervention.

## Not in this PR

- The `_index.md` files are removed and do not return; the consolidated files are now the navigation.
- Companion dual-layout support for the portal and the review tool is prepared separately, so both read either layout across the cutover.
- A document-order assertion for `atlas-validator` is a separate PR: consolidation removes a guarantee the filesystem used to provide for free — a document could not be out of order or in another Star's file — and the validator does not currently check it.
